import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Order the sensor types by their median price for better readability and insight
# This helps in quickly identifying which sensor types are generally more expensive
order = df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index

# Create a violin plot to show the distribution of prices across different sensor types.
# Violin plots are excellent for visualizing the distribution (density, spread, and central tendency)
# of a continuous variable across different categories.
sns.violinplot(
    data=df,
    x='sensor_type',
    y='price_usd',
    order=order,
    inner='quartile',  # Shows the quartiles (median, 25th, 75th percentile) inside the violins
    linewidth=1.0      # Adjust line width for better visual clarity
)

# Add labels and title for clarity
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Prices by Sensor Type', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# Rotate x-axis labels if they are long to prevent overlapping
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a subtle grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Improve layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
